edge.title: The government deadline that arrives with a link
edge.setup: Ration card e-KYC is due soon. A message or a helpful stranger says it must be done today, shares a link or app, and mentions a small 'processing fee' or asks for an OTP to 'complete verification'.
edge.tell: A real deadline, delivered through a channel you did not open yourself, asking for money or an OTP.
move: Do not tap the link or share any OTP. Go to the department's own website or office, which you reach yourself.
Check the deadline on the official notice, not in the message that is pushing you.
If you already shared an OTP or paid, call your bank and the 1930 cybercrime helpline now.
edge.why: Scammers do not need to invent urgency when a real deadline already exists. They ride on it. The deadline is true; the channel is the fake. So judge who contacted whom, not whether the deadline is real.
edge.variants: Same shape: PAN-Aadhaar linking 'last date' texts, FASTag KYC calls, electricity 'disconnection tonight' messages, bank KYC-update links.

lens.name: Goodhart's Law
lens.one_line: When a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring what it used to.
lens.detail: Any number used to judge people will be optimised directly, often by routes that bypass the thing the number was standing in for. Not usually by cheating — by honest, rational effort aimed at the metric rather than the goal, because the metric is what's rewarded.
elsewhere: Police judged on cases closed may book easier cases and discourage hard complaints.
Schools judged on pass rates quietly move weak students out before the exam.
Support teams judged on ticket-closing time close tickets fast, unresolved.
lens.test: What number are these people judged on, and what's the cheapest way to move it that doesn't involve doing the actual job?
lens.today: Country and Politics reports Bengaluru Traffic Police logged 601 drunk-driving cases and 240 overspeeding violations in a week-long special drive. I only have the headline, but the number is a useful reminder: a drive is judged by the count of cases, so it rewards where checking is easy, not necessarily where the risk is highest. Read such totals as a sign of where enforcement looked, not as a measure of how safe the roads are.
